chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'Is it permissible to sell the palm tree when it has borne fruit?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Its sale is permissible until it is in splendour.' I said, 'And what is the splendour? May I be sacrificed for you.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'When it turns red and yellow, and similar to that.'

key_terms.يَزْهُوَ: To be in splendour / reach maturity

ai.seo_question: When is the optimal time to sell a fruit-bearing palm tree according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the specific temporal boundary for valid sales of unharvested fruit, defining 'zahu' not merely as flowering but as the visible color change (reddening and yellowing) that signals ripeness. This definition prevents ambiguity in commercial transactions by anchoring the legal concept of maturity to observable physical signs, a principle widely cited in Shia fiqh to ensure fairness and prevent dispute in agricultural trade.
